co/investors/zero_infinity_partners) joined the round, which ranks among the largest seed rounds ever for a US transportation and energy startup — above the 97th percentile. **How it works:** The year-old company provides hardware and software that remotely switches on backup generators when grids face emergencies. That displaces demand at those sites, freeing up power for the rest of the grid. Its system works with diesel and gas generators and batteries. **Why now?** Power demand is rising fast, straining grids and pushing up electricity bills, while new power plants remain slow and costly to build. AGent targets the generators that sit mostly idle at farms, hospitals, factories, big-box stores, and universities. **What's the endgame?** AGent works with grid operators and utilities to supply extra capacity, sharing revenue with generator owners. It already operates in three markets — Texas (ERCOT), the Midcontinent Independent System Operator region, and PJM — with a portfolio the size of a small power plant.
